label: Real estate agent
seoTitle: Real Estate Agent Email Signature: Examples and What to Include
metaDescription: Real estate agent and realtor email signature examples with licence number, brokerage, booking button and disclaimer. Build yours from your brokerage website.
heading: Real Estate Agent Email Signature Examples
shortAnswer: A real estate agent's email signature should show your name, your licence number and brokerage where your state or brokerage requires them, one phone number, and a single booking or listings link. Add a short Equal Housing Opportunity line in the US, and leave out quotes, awards lists and more than three social icons.
description: Buyers and sellers read agent emails on their phones, often between viewings. A good signature makes the next step obvious, which is usually to call you or book a time, and carries the details your licence rules ask for without turning into a wall of small print.
keywords: real estate agent email signature, realtor email signature, real estate email signature
include: Your full name and a title buyers understand, such as Sales Agent or Associate Broker.
Your licence number and state, if your state or brokerage requires it in advertising. Many do, and email can count as advertising.
Your brokerage name. Most brokerages require it on anything you send to clients.
One mobile number, written in full international format if you work with overseas buyers.
One call to action: book a viewing, see current listings, or get a free appraisal.
A short Equal Housing Opportunity line or logo in the US.
avoid: Use REALTOR® only if you are a member of the National Association of Realtors. It is a registered membership mark, not a job title.
Do not list every award, designation and sales figure. Pick the one a buyer will recognise.
Skip large listing photos in the signature. They get clipped in replies and blocked by many inboxes.
Do not use three different phone numbers. Clients will call the wrong one.

examples.title: Agent with a booking button
examples.why: The filled button gives clients one obvious next step, and the licence details sit underneath in small print.

examples.title: Brokerage-branded signature
examples.why: When your brokerage has a strong logo and colour, lead with it. Clients often remember the brokerage before they remember you.

examples.title: Phone-first for open homes
examples.why: Buyers at an open home want to call, not click. The phone number comes first and is labelled, so it is one tap on a phone.

faqs.q: Do real estate agents have to put their licence number in their email signature?
faqs.a: It depends on your state and your brokerage. Many US states require a licence number or brokerage name in advertising, and some treat email to the public as advertising. Check your state real estate commission's rules and your brokerage's policy. The generator's compliance fields add the licence number, state and brokerage under your signature.

faqs.q: Can I call myself a REALTOR® in my signature?
faqs.a: Only if you are a member of the National Association of Realtors. REALTOR® is a registered membership mark. If you are not a member, use a plain title such as Sales Agent, Real Estate Agent or Associate Broker.

faqs.q: Should I put listing photos in my email signature?
faqs.a: No. Large images are often blocked, clipped in replies or flagged as promotional. Link to your current listings with a button instead, and keep the signature to your headshot or brokerage logo.

faqs.q: What is the best call to action for a real estate signature?
faqs.a: Use one. Book a viewing, see my listings or get a free appraisal all work. More than one link competes for attention and none of them get clicked.

label: Nurse
seoTitle: Nurse Email Signature: Credentials Order and Examples
metaDescription: Nurse email signature examples with credentials in the right order, unit and contact details, and a confidentiality notice. Build yours free to preview.
heading: Nurse Email Signature Examples and Credentials Order
shortAnswer: A nurse's email signature should give your name, then credentials in the order the American Nurses Credentialing Center recommends (highest degree, licensure, state designations, national certifications, awards, other), your role and unit, your facility and a work phone. Never put patient information in email, and do not rely on a disclaimer to make email secure.
description: Nurses email managers, colleagues on other shifts, educators and sometimes patients' families. The signature has two jobs: show your credentials correctly, and tell people the fastest way to reach your unit. Most of the mistakes are in the order of letters after your name.
keywords: nurse email signature, nursing email signature, rn email signature, nurse credentials email signature
include: Your name followed by credentials in the recommended order, for example Jane Doe, MSN, RN, CCRN.
Your role and unit, such as Charge Nurse, Cardiac ICU.
Your hospital, clinic or health system name.
A work phone or unit extension. Leave out your personal mobile unless your employer asks for it.
A short confidentiality notice if your employer requires one.
Pronouns, if you want to include them.
avoid: Do not list every course certificate. Keep national certifications and leave internal training off.
Never include patient names, dates or other health details in email, signature or not.
Do not use a decorative font for credentials. Letters like RN and CNL must be easy to read.
Avoid inspirational quotes. They look out of place in clinical email.

examples.title: Hospital nurse with credentials
examples.why: Credentials follow the recommended order and the unit is named, so colleagues know exactly who they are emailing.

examples.title: Nurse practitioner in a clinic
examples.why: A clean, photo-free layout suits clinical email, and the plain contact line keeps it short in long reply chains.

examples.title: Nurse educator
examples.why: Educators often email students and new graduates, so a friendly headshot and a clear title help people put a face to the name.

faqs.q: What order should nursing credentials go in an email signature?
faqs.a: The American Nurses Credentialing Center recommends: highest earned degree, then licensure (such as RN or APRN), state designations, national certifications (such as CCRN), awards and honours, and other recognitions. For example: Jane Doe, MSN, RN, CCRN.

faqs.q: Should a nurse include a HIPAA notice in their email signature?
faqs.a: Include one if your employer requires it. A notice does not make email secure or compliant on its own, so never send patient information in ordinary email. The generator can add a short confidentiality notice under your signature.

faqs.q: Can I put my RN licence number in my signature?
faqs.a: You can, and some employers or roles ask for it, but most nurses do not need to. If you add it, the generator's compliance fields place it in small print under your contact details.

label: Lawyer
seoTitle: Lawyer Email Signature: Examples, Disclaimers and Bar Details
metaDescription: Lawyer and attorney email signature examples with firm details, bar admission and a confidentiality notice. See what to include and build yours from your firm's website.
heading: Lawyer Email Signature Examples
shortAnswer: A lawyer's email signature should show your name, title, firm, direct phone and office address, and your bar admissions if your jurisdiction expects them. A short confidentiality notice is common, but keep it under three lines and check your state's advertising rules, since some require extra wording on marketing emails.
description: Clients judge a firm by small details, and the signature is one of the few things they see on every email. A good lawyer's signature is formal, easy to read on a phone and short enough that the confidentiality notice does not outweigh the message.
keywords: lawyer email signature, attorney email signature, law firm email signature, legal email disclaimer
include: Your full name and title, such as Partner, Associate or Of Counsel.
Your firm name and office address, which many state bars expect on lawyer communications.
A direct phone line and your email.
Bar admissions or your bar number, where your jurisdiction or firm requires it.
A short confidentiality notice if your firm uses one.
Attorney Advertising wording on marketing emails, if your state requires it.
avoid: Do not use a ten-line disclaimer. Courts give boilerplate little weight, and clients stop reading.
Avoid inspirational quotes, emojis and bright colours. Formality is part of the message.
Do not claim to be a specialist or expert unless your state bar certifies you as one.
Leave out personal social accounts. Link to the firm's LinkedIn page if anything.

examples.title: Partner with bar details and notice
examples.why: A formal layout with a vertical rule, bar admission and a short confidentiality notice under the contact details.

examples.title: Associate at a small firm
examples.why: The letterhead layout echoes printed firm stationery and highlights the firm name in its brand colour.

examples.title: Solo practitioner, plain text
examples.why: A text-only signature never breaks, never gets blocked and reads the same in every client, which suits court and government correspondence.

faqs.q: Do lawyers need a disclaimer in their email signature?
faqs.a: Usually it is firm policy rather than a legal requirement. A short confidentiality notice is common practice, but courts give boilerplate little weight, so it does not replace care about who you email. Some states require Attorney Advertising wording on marketing emails, so check your state bar's rules.

faqs.q: Should I put my bar number in my email signature?
faqs.a: Some jurisdictions and firms expect bar admissions or a bar number on lawyer communications, and many lawyers list their admitted states. The generator's compliance fields add a bar number and state in small print under your details.

faqs.q: What is the best email signature format for a law firm?
faqs.a: A formal layout with name, title, firm, direct line, office address and one link to the firm's website. Use the firm's colour sparingly, avoid images other than the logo, and keep any notice to two or three lines.

label: Graduate student
seoTitle: Graduate Student Email Signature: Examples for Master's and Grad School
metaDescription: Graduate student email signature examples for master's students, research assistants and teaching assistants. See what to include, how to write your degree, and what to leave out.
heading: Graduate Student Email Signature Examples
shortAnswer: A graduate student email signature should show your full name, your degree and field written as a candidate or student (for example MS Candidate, Mechanical Engineering), your department and university, and one way to reach you. Add your assistantship title if you email as a TA or RA, and leave the degree letters off your name until the degree is awarded.
description: Grad students email professors, students they teach, collaborators at other universities and employers, sometimes in the same afternoon. A good signature tells each of them what you study and in what capacity you are writing, in three or four lines.
keywords: graduate student email signature, grad student email signature, masters student email signature
note: Title and degree wording on this page is general guidance. Your university, program or employer may set its own signature format, so check their style guide first.

cta.heading: Build your graduate student signature
cta.text: Start with a simple layout, add your degree, department and university, and see it update as you type.

related.label: Student email signature examples for college, internships and recent graduates

include: Your full name, as it appears on your university record or the name you publish under.
Your degree and field, written as a student or candidate: MS Candidate, Mechanical Engineering, or Master of Public Health student.
Your department or school, then the university name.
Your assistantship title when you write in that role, such as Graduate Teaching Assistant or Graduate Research Assistant.
Your university email address. Add a phone number only if you want calls from the people you are writing to.
One link that helps the reader: LinkedIn for job searches, or a lab or portfolio page for research contacts.
Your expected graduation date when you are applying for jobs or internships.
avoid: Do not put MS, MA or MBA after your name until the degree has been awarded. Before that, write Candidate or student.
Leave out your GPA, coursework and awards. Those belong on your resume.
Skip inspirational quotes and personal social media accounts.
Check your university brand rules before using the logo or seal. Many universities limit them to official communications.
Do not list every role you hold. Use the one that matches the email you are sending.

examples.title: Master's student, everyday email
examples.why: Four lines cover who you are, what you study and how to reply. It works for professors, administrators and classmates.

examples.title: Graduate teaching assistant
examples.why: Students need to know which course you teach and how to reach you, so the title names the course and the department comes second.

examples.title: Research assistant writing to collaborators
examples.why: People outside your university want to know which lab you work in. The lab name sits with the university and the link goes to the lab page.

data.title: Graduate Research Assistant
data.company: Coastal Ecology Lab, Riverside State University

faqs.q: How do I write a master's degree in progress in my email signature?
faqs.a: Write the degree as a candidate or student, followed by your field: MS Candidate, Computer Science, or Master of Social Work student. Do not put the degree letters after your name until the degree has been awarded.

faqs.q: Should I list both my TA and RA roles?
faqs.a: No. Use the role you are writing in. Use the teaching assistant title when you email students in your course, and the research assistant title when you email collaborators. Most email clients let you save more than one signature.

faqs.q: Should a graduate student email signature include a phone number?
faqs.a: Only if you want the people you email to call you. For most academic email, your university address is enough. Add a mobile number when you are job hunting or coordinating fieldwork.

faqs.q: Can I include my bachelor's degree after my name?
faqs.a: You can, but it is unusual in the United States. Most graduate students list only the degree they are working toward. If you hold a professional licence or certification that matters to the reader, that is more useful than a bachelor's degree.

label: PhD student
seoTitle: PhD Student Email Signature: Examples for Students and Candidates
metaDescription: PhD student and PhD candidate email signature examples. See when to write Student or Candidate, how to list your lab and department, and what to leave out.
heading: PhD Student Email Signature Examples
shortAnswer: A PhD student email signature should show your full name, PhD Student or PhD Candidate with your field, your department and university, and your university email. Write Candidate only after you have advanced to candidacy, and do not use Dr or put PhD after your name until the degree is awarded.
description: Doctoral students write to supervisors, journal editors, conference organisers and researchers they have never met. The signature is often the only introduction they get, so it should say what you research and where, without claiming a title you do not hold yet.
keywords: phd student email signature, phd candidate email signature, doctoral student email signature
note: Title and degree wording on this page is general guidance. Your university, program or employer may set its own signature format, so check their style guide first.

cta.heading: Build your PhD student signature
cta.text: Start with a plain layout, add your field, lab and university, and see it update as you type.

related.label: Student email signature examples for college, internships and recent graduates

include: Your full name, matching the name you publish under.
PhD Student or PhD Candidate, followed by your field.
Your department, then the university.
Your lab or research group when you write to people outside your department.
Your university email address.
One research link: your lab page, a personal academic site, Google Scholar or your ORCID record.
Your teaching or research assistant title when you write in that role.
avoid: Do not use Dr or put PhD after your name before the degree is awarded.
Do not write PhD Candidate before you have advanced to candidacy. At most US universities that means passing qualifying exams and having a proposal approved. Until then, write PhD Student.
ABD (all but dissertation) is informal. Leave it out of a signature.
Do not list publications, grants or awards. Link to a page that has them.
Skip quotes and long lists of pronoun, land or availability statements unless your department asks for them.

examples.title: PhD candidate, everyday email
examples.why: Name, stage, field and institution in three lines. Editors and other researchers can place you at a glance.

examples.title: First-year PhD student
examples.why: Before candidacy the accurate title is PhD Student. The text-only layout survives every email client and reply chain.

examples.title: Candidate on the job market
examples.why: When you are applying for postdocs or industry roles, add a phone number and a link to your academic site with your CV and papers.

faqs.q: What is the difference between PhD Student and PhD Candidate in a signature?
faqs.a: A PhD student is enrolled in a doctoral program. A PhD candidate has advanced to candidacy, which at most US universities means finishing coursework, passing qualifying exams and having a dissertation proposal approved. Use the title that matches your current status, and check how your program defines candidacy.

faqs.q: Can I put PhD(c) or ABD after my name?
faqs.a: It is better not to. PhD(c) and ABD are informal and many academics read them as overstating your status. Write PhD Candidate on the title line instead.

faqs.q: Should I include my ORCID or Google Scholar link?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have published or are submitting work. Use one research link, not three. An ORCID record or a personal academic site is the most stable choice because it stays the same when you change university.

faqs.q: When can I start using Dr in my email signature?
faqs.a: After your degree has been conferred. Some people start after a successful defence and final submission, but the safe rule is to wait for the university to award the degree.

label: Medical student
seoTitle: Medical Student Email Signature: MD Candidate Examples
metaDescription: Medical student email signature examples for MD and DO candidates. See how to write your class year, what to use on rotations, and why to leave off Dr and MD.
heading: Medical Student Email Signature Examples
shortAnswer: A medical student email signature should show your full name, MD Candidate or DO Candidate with your class year, your medical school, and your school email. Do not use Dr or put MD or DO after your name until you graduate, and make it clear you are a student when you email patients, preceptors or clinical staff.
description: Medical students email deans, residents, attendings, research mentors and residency programs. The signature has two jobs: say which school and class you are in, and make it plain that you are a student and not yet a physician.
keywords: medical student email signature, md candidate email signature, med student email signature
note: Title and degree wording on this page is general guidance. Your university, program or employer may set its own signature format, so check their style guide first.

cta.heading: Build your medical student signature
cta.text: Start with a plain layout, add MD Candidate, your class year and school, and see it update as you type.

related.label: Student email signature examples for college, internships and recent graduates

include: Your full name.
MD Candidate or DO Candidate, followed by your class year: MD Candidate, Class of 2028.
Your medical school name in full.
Your school email address. Use it for anything related to clinical work.
A phone number during clinical years, when residents and coordinators need to reach you quickly.
A leadership or research role when you write in that capacity, such as a student organisation office or a named lab.
A degree you already hold, such as MPH or PhD, may follow your name.
avoid: Do not use Dr, MD or DO before graduation. It can mislead patients and staff about who is treating them.
Avoid MS3 or M2 when you write to people outside medicine. MS also means Master of Science. Write Third-Year Medical Student or your class year.
Do not add a hospital logo or name unless the hospital has told you to. You are a student of the school, not an employee of the site.
Do not add your own confidentiality notice. If your school or clinical site supplies one, use theirs word for word.
Leave out board scores, class rank and honours.

examples.why: Name, degree in progress, class year and school. It is enough for faculty, administrators and research mentors.

examples.title: Clinical rotations
examples.why: On the wards, people need to know you are a student and how to page or call you. The title says so in plain words and the phone number comes next.

examples.title: DO student with a research role
examples.why: When you write to journals or collaborators, lead with the research role and keep the degree line. A prior degree can follow your name.

data.title: DO Candidate, Class of 2028 | Student Researcher

faqs.q: How do I write MD Candidate in an email signature?
faqs.a: Put it on the line under your name with your class year: MD Candidate, Class of 2028. Osteopathic students write DO Candidate. Put your medical school on the next line.

faqs.q: Can a medical student use Dr or Student Doctor in a signature?
faqs.a: Do not use Dr before you graduate. Some schools use Student Doctor on the wards, and some forbid it. In writing, Medical Student or MD Candidate is clearer, so use that unless your school tells you otherwise.

faqs.q: Should I put MS3 or my class year?
faqs.a: Use your class year, or write out Third-Year Medical Student. MS3 and M3 are understood inside medical schools, but outside them MS reads as Master of Science.

faqs.q: Do I need a HIPAA confidentiality notice?
faqs.a: Not one you write yourself. If your school or clinical site requires a notice, they will give you the wording. Either way, do not send patient information from a personal email account.

shortAnswer: A law student email signature should show your full name, J.D. Candidate with your class year, your law school, and your email and phone. Add one journal, moot court or clinic role if it matters to the reader. Do not use Esq., Attorney or anything that suggests you are admitted to practice.
description: Law students write to professors, recruiters, judges' chambers and practising lawyers, and those readers notice small things. A plain, accurate signature shows your school and class year and makes no claim to a licence you do not have yet.
keywords: law student email signature, jd candidate email signature, law school email signature
note: Title and degree wording on this page is general guidance. Your university, program or employer may set its own signature format, so check their style guide first.

examples.why: At a firm, the title must show you are not yet a lawyer. Summer Associate or Law Clerk does that, and the firm name replaces your school.

faqs.q: How do I write J.D. Candidate in an email signature?
faqs.a: Put it under your name with your class year: J.D. Candidate, Class of 2027. Both J.D. and JD are accepted. Use whichever your law school uses, and keep it the same on your resume.

faqs.q: Can a law student use Esq.?
faqs.a: No. Esq. is used in the United States by lawyers who are admitted to practise. Using it as a student can suggest you are licensed, and bar authorities take that seriously.

faqs.q: What should my signature say while I wait for bar results?
faqs.a: Use the title your employer gives you, such as Law Clerk or Associate with a note that you are not yet admitted. Many firms have set wording for this. Do not use Attorney or Esq. until you are sworn in.

faqs.q: Should I list law review in my signature?
faqs.a: Yes, if you hold a position on it and you are writing to employers or academics. Keep it to one line next to your class year, and remove it when the position ends.
